Ivana M. Rossi is a Senior Financial Sector Expert at the IMF’s Legal Department Financial Integrity Group (FIG). She has over 20 years of experience working in the areas of financial integrity, illicit financial flows, and anti-corruption, and has provided tailored technical assistance to dozens of countries worldwide, on AML/CFT, beneficial ownership transparency, and anti corruption reforms, and served as a FATF assessor. Prior to joining the IMF in 2018, she worked at the World Bank Group and the Stolen Asset Recovery Initiative (StAR) for over a decade, where she led global work on financial disclosure by public officials and supported countries in combating illicit financial flows. Ms. Rossi has several publications and is a frequent speaker at international fora on integrity, transparency, and financial crime.
Jacob Sims: Jacob Sims is a Visiting Fellow at Harvard University's Asia Center and an expert on transnational crime and corruption. He led one of the first teams responding to Cambodia's scam-compound crisis; was a co-author of USIP's 2024 Senior Study Group on transnational crime; and authored the 2025 USAID-funded study Policies and Patterns. He advises congressional committees, government agencies, international organizations, NGOs and private-sector actors on digital era criminal-autocratic threats.

Janice is currently A Global Law student at Bocconi University in Milan where she works at the intersection of law, artificial intelligence, civic education, and democratic governance. Her anti-corruption advocacy began in her teens, earning presidential recognition at 17 for mobilising young people against corruption.

Jayaram Venkatesan: Jayaram Venkatesan holds an MS in Electrical Engineering from the University of Cincinnati, USA, and previously worked as Vice President at Countrywide Securities Research, Los Angeles. Leaving behind a successful corporate career, he returned to India to pursue his passion for social change. He is the co-founder and Convener of Arappor Iyakkam, a people’s movement in Tamil Nadu dedicated to building a just and transparent society. Despite facing severe threats and resistance, Arappor Iyakkam has spearheaded the fight against Corruption in TamilNadu India in various issues such as poor roads, housing for the poorest, Electricity scams and many others. Jelter Meers:
Workshop Coordinator for Exposing and Removing the Barriers to Protecting our Oceans (8.7)

Jelter Meers is the data and research editor of the Pulitzer Center. He started as an investigative reporter at the Midwest Center for Investigative Reporting in Illinois, where he wrote accountability stories on housing, migrant labor, and big agriculture. After reporting on human trafficking and the migrant crisis in Europe, he began to specialize in organized crime and joined the Organized Crime and Corruption Reporting Project in 2018 as a daily news reporter and then as a researcher. In 2020, he became the global network’s coordinating editor.

As a reporter, researcher and editor, he worked on projects such as Dubai’s Golden Sands, the Troika Laundromat, the FinCEN Files, and Blowing Unsmoke, using his expertise to uncover hidden assets, international money trails, offshore company ownership, and transnational organized crime groups.

Jezabel Pando: Jezabel Pando is a Paraguayan executive and lawyer with experience in corporate governance, risk, regulatory affairs, and business integrity. She serves as General Counsel and Head of Legal and Corporate Affairs at CADIEM. Alongside her organizational role, she chairs the Advisory Group of Alliance for Integrity in Paraguay and represents the private sector alternate member on its Global Steering Committee. Her experience spans highly regulated industries, where she has led organizational transformation and Collective Action initiatives, with a particular focus on translating integrity standards into practical solutions and capabilities for SMEs. She holds a Master’s degree in Compliance and is certified as Organizational Systemic Coach, combining legal rigor, strategic thinking, and a human understanding of how organizations change.
Jim Mintz:
Workshop Coordinator and Rapporteur for Playing a Game to Expose Corruption (5.8)

Jim Mintz has spent his life conducting investigations and training investigators all over the world.   The game Kleptocrat:  How To Hide Dirty Money was created at Mintz Group, the private-investigation company that Jim ran until his retirement.   Jim now teaches investigative reporting at Columbia Journalism School.   Also, in Berlin, he founded Seek Initiative to help citizens dig into wrongdoing.

Joanna Choblet:
Workshop Coordinator for Real-World Integrity Solutions for SIDS: Experiences from climate and disaster operations (2.4)

Joanna Choblet is a Policy Officer at the Wildlife Justice Commission, an organisation dedicated to disrupting and dismantling transnational criminal networks trafficking wildlife, fish and timber. In this role, she translates evidence from investigations into policy recommendations and engages in international processes on environmental crimes and their convergence with corruption, financial crime and other forms of organised crime, supporting governments in strengthening legal and enforcement responses.

She also supports the Wildlife Justice Commission’s chairing of the Working Group on Environmental Crime and Corruption of the Global Civil Society Coalition for the UN Convention against Corruption (UNCAC), which represents more than 280 civil society members worldwide.

Joanna holds two Master’s degrees, both awarded cum laude, from Leiden University (LL.M. Public International Law; MSc Comparative Criminal Justice), an LL.B. from Perpignan and Örebro Universities, and a Diploma in Animal Law from Åbo Akademi University.
Joanna Kao:
Workshop Coordinator for Scaling Public Sector AI with Accountability (2.6)

Workshop Coordinator for From Stories to Action: Can Young Creators Hold Power Accountable? (2.7)

Workshop Coordinator for Investigating Big Tech's Environmental Impact (7.6)

Joanna S. Kao leads the Pulitzer Center's AI Accountability Network, where she oversees a portfolio of AI and machine-learning reporting projects and aims to foster a growing, global community of journalists doing AI-related reporting.

She was previously the tech lead of the Financial Times' visual and data journalism team and a multimedia reporter and interactive developer at Al Jazeera America.

In 2023, she was named a Pulitzer Center AI Accountability Fellow, reporting on how artificial intelligence has helped and hurt disabled people.

She has taught data visualization at Columbia Journalism School, as well as developed and taught two new accessibility courses for The New School Parsons School of Design. She also co-authored an academic book chapter on integrating data processes in newsrooms.

Kao holds a computer science degree from MIT and a master of business administration from IE Business School.
Jodi Vittori:
Workshop Coordinator for Security Guarantees, Resource Contracts, and Corruption (6.3)

Jodi Vittori is an expert on the linkages of corruption, state fragility, illicit finance, and US national security. She is a Professor of Practice and co-chair of the Global Politics and Security program at Georgetown University’s School of Foreign Service. Jodi is also an associate fellow with RUSI’s Centre for Finance and Security and was previously a non-resident fellow with the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace. Before joining the Georgetown University faculty, she was the US Research and Policy Manager for Transparency International’s Defense and Security Program and a senior policy advisor for Global Witness. Jodi also served in the U.S. Air Force and she was assigned to NATO’s only counter-corruption task force. She was an Assistant Professor and military faculty at the US Air Force Academy and the National Defense University. Jodi is a founder and co-moderator of the Anti-Corruption Advocacy Network (ACAN).
Jodie Ginsberg: Jodie Ginsberg is the chief executive officer of the Committee to Protect Journalists. A journalist by profession, Ginsberg joined CPJ in 2022 from Internews Europe, where she was chief executive officer. Ginsberg began her career as a graduate trainee with Reuters news agency and worked as a commodities reporter in London before taking up a posting as a foreign correspondent in Johannesburg, South Africa. She subsequently worked as Reuters’ chief correspondent in Ireland, and then bureau chief for the U.K. and Ireland. In 2014, Ginsberg was appointed chief executive of London-based freedom of expression group Index on Censorship, which she led until 2020. An internationally respected campaigner on issues of media freedom and freedom of expression, Ginsberg is a regular speaker on journalist safety and issues involving access to information. She serves on the boards of The Trust for the Bureau of Investigative Journalism, the John S. Knight Journalism Fellowships at Stanford, and as a Council member of IFEX, the international network for freedom of expression organizations. Ginsberg has a BA in English Literature from the University of Cambridge and a postgraduate diploma in newspaper journalism from City St George’s, University of London.

Jojo Mehta:
Jojo Mehta co-founded Stop Ecocide in 2017, alongside barrister and legal pioneer the late Polly Higgins, to support the establishment of ecocide as a crime at the International Criminal Court.

As CEO and key spokesperson, she has overseen the remarkable growth of the movement while coordinating between legal developments, diplomatic traction and public narrative.

She is Chair of the charitable Stop Ecocide Foundation and convenor of the Independent Expert Panel for the Legal Definition of Ecocide chaired by Philippe Sands KC and Dior Fall Sow. The resulting definition, launched in June 2021, has catalysed legislative developments, recommendations and resolutions at national, regional and international levels.

Jojo is a graduate of Oxford and London universities and has a background in communications, entrepreneurship and on-the-ground environmental campaigning. With a natural ability to connect and inspire, coupled with an unshakeable faith in the human imagination and capacity for positive change, she has contributed to UN conferences, diplomatic events, law and business summits as well as podcasts, interviews and articles for publications and broadcasters ranging from TIME Magazine to the New York Times and from The Guardian to the BBC.

With representation and associate teams now in over 45 countries, Stop Ecocide International generates fertile collaborations at diplomatic and political level, as well as across civil society with lawyers, academics, corporate influencers, indigenous and faith leaders, NGOs and grassroots campaigns.

As a result, legal recognition of ecocide is emerging as a powerful driver of change and a key solution addressing the climate and ecological crisis.

Jonatan Rodríguez:

Jonatan Rodríguez is a Colombian sociologist and development professional with 12 years of experience in impact, communications, and audience engagement. As Senior Program Manager at the Pulitzer Center, he leads strategies to expand the reach and impact of investigative journalism across Latin America. His work focuses on connecting journalism with communities, civil society, and institutions to advance public engagement and accountability. Previously, he was Colombia Country Manager at Change.org and Latin America Editor at openDemocracy.
Jonathan Bourguignon:
Workshop Coordinator for Anti-Corruption as Conflict Prevention: Lessons Learned from Conflict-affected Settings (4.3)

Jonathan leads UNODC’s portfolio on addressing corruption in fragile and conflict-affected settings. Since joining the UN, he has supported anti-corruption field engagement and partnerships with various UN Missions, including in Central African Republic, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Haiti, Mali and Somalia. His wider work at UN Headquarters focuses on corruption, economic crime and illicit financial flows, in support of policy discussions at UN Headquarters and technical assistance delivery of field offices.

Joseph Whittal: Mr. Joseph Akanjolenur Whittal, Commissioner of the Commission on Human Rights and Administrative Justice (CHRAJ), and Chair of the Governing Council with supervisory oversight of all functions of CHRAJ, was appointed Commissioner in December 2016. Prior to his appointment, Mr. Whittal had since 2012 served as a Deputy Commissioner in charge of Legal and Investigations for the Commission. He first joined the Commission in 1994 as Upper East Regional Director, and was later appointed Director, Legal and Investigations at the Head Office between 2008 and 2012. Commissioner Whittal who is currently the Chairman of the Working Group (WG) of the Network of African National Human Rights Institutions on the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), and the African Agenda 2063, is also the Vice Chairman of the Network of African National Human Rights Institutions (NANHRI), elected at the 13th Biennial Conference of the 44 Member Network of African Human Rights Institutions on the Continent. Mr. Whittal is responsible for Coordinating International Co-operation with International Human Rights Organisations such as United Nations Special Procedures and Mechanisms: Special Rapporteur on thematic issues; Treaty-based Committees, Preparation of CHRAJ’s Independent Report on the Universal Periodic Review (UPR) to the Human Rights Council (HRC); and the International Coordinating Committee (ICC) of the National Human Rights Institutions; the Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR). His schedule also demands the Coordination of Regional Cooperation with the African Commission on Human and People’s Rights (ACHPR); African Court on Human Rights; ECOWAS Community Court; the Network of African National Human Rights Institutions (NANHRI), bilateral relations with other National Human Rights Institutions (NHRIs), International Cooperation with the International Ombudsman Institute (IOI); the African Ombudsman and Mediators Association (AOMA), and bilateral relations with other Ombudsman Institutions. Mr. Whittal, a Doctoral Candidate at the Doctor of Business Leadership (DBL) of the prestigious Paris-based IPAG Business School/Nobel International Business School, has been elected Bureau Member (Member of the Governing Board) of the Geneva-based Global Alliance of National Human Rights Institutions (GANHRI), representing the Network of African National Human Rights Institutions on the World Body. Mr. Whittal has honoured speaking engagements within and outside Ghana on any of the triple mandates of the Commission: Human Rights, Administrative Justice and Anti- Corruption, as well as on general governance issues during conferences, workshops, seminars, among others. He is a Member of the Board of the Data Protection Commission (DPC) of Ghana
Juan Carlos Buitrago Arias: Juan Carlos Buitrago Arias is a regional and international authority on public security, organized crime, and strategic foresight, with more than three decades of service to Colombia. He holds an Honorary Doctorate (2024) from the Mexican Institute of Leaders of Excellence and is a Certified BASC Auditor. He served as Director of Operations of the National Intelligence Agency and Director of the Fiscal and Customs Police of Colombia. He is the Founder and CEO of Strategos BIP and CIMA (Central de Investigación sobre Comercio Ilícito), and coordinates the “Triángulos Strategy,” a public-private alliance combating illicit trade and criminal networks across Latin America and the Caribbean. He currently leads the Panama Customs Modernization Program and serves as GRANTI Advisor for INL USA Guatemala. Author of six books on organized crime, security, and governance, and a columnist for El Tiempo and Las2Orillas. He has lectured in more than 20 countries and is a member of the Expert Panel of GLACSED (Latin American and Caribbean Group on Security and Democracy).
